subject: english
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Share and explain their ideas and viewpoints in class
Ask and answer questions on a topic
Interpret and analyse content, and draw conclusions from key details
Use material from other sources, such as the internet, to reinforce what is taught
Understand the speaker's message, both spoken and unspoken (body language, expression)
Connect ideas from texts to their own life, comparing information
Use gestures, eye contact, clear pace, and suitable tone, stress and intonation
Take dictation of an unseen passage
Identify the main aspects and broad outline of a text, and explain events and why they happened, using key details
Link opinions and reasons with words, phrases and clauses
Work out the meaning of words and figurative language, such as similes
Use technology to gather information for a project presentation
Write at least two paragraphs of about 150 words on a given topic
Write narratives with details of actions, thoughts and feelings, linked with 'firstly', 'then', 'later' and 'finally'
Write short notes and write-ups from their own experience on self-concept, respect for diversity and responsible behaviour
Follow the writing process: plan, write, revise, edit and rewrite
Use vocabulary suited to different registers, such as cookery, yoga or sports
Use adverbs, conjunctions, prepositions and interjections, and the kinds of adverbs
Learn the meaning and use of common idioms and proverbs
Use plural possessives, comparisons of adjectives and adverbs, and contractions such as 'can't' and 'won't'
Use irregular verbs in simple and continuous tenses, such as break, broke, broken
Spell commonly used words correctly
Use direct and reported speech in dialogue
Make the subject and verb agree at a higher level
